preamble: The voiced palatalized bilabial stop [bʲ] becomes voiceless [pʲ] while keeping its palatalization when a language combines word-final soft labials with final devoicing. Russian is the clear case: soft [bʲ] in голубя (gen.) alternates with final [pʲ] in голубь [ˈɡoɫʊpʲ], and дроби with дробь [dropʲ]. Most other Slavic languages hardened final soft labials before devoicing, so they show plain [p] instead (Polish gołąb /ˈɡɔwɔmp/, gen. gołębia; Belarusian голуб [ˈɣoɫup]; Czech holub [ˈɦolup]).

examples.note: Word-final devoicing turns soft [bʲ] into [pʲ] without loss of palatalization.
